links.note: Was 32735 (Condensation Defined). Recording the reading every five minutes for thirty is Activity 8.4, the weighing that makes the vapour measurable, in 32736.
Was 32747 (Explaining Everyday Observations), the exercise set. Repeating the activity on a windy or rainy day is an instruction inside Activity 8.8, in 32742.
Was 32746 (The Water Cycle). Squeezing the bottle and watching the space above the water - with and without the burnt paper - is Activity 8.10 in 32745, the cloud-needs-dust demonstration.
Was 32744 (A Pot-in-Pot Cooler). Natural grass feeling cooler than plastic grass is answered by the cooling effect of evaporation, which is 32743; 32744 is only the sand-and-pots device.
Was 32746 (The Water Cycle), which is the circulation of water and has no liquids other than water in it. Naming other liquids that evaporate is an open exercise, listed in 32747.
Was 32748 (Things to Make and Act Out), whose blow-on-a-wet-hand demo is a different item. Why a fan dries clothes although fans cool things is one of 32747's explain-this exercises.
Was 32746 (The Water Cycle). Which condition makes water evaporate faster is the sun/wind/humidity finding of 32742.
Was 32731 (Ice and Water Are One Substance). Why droplets appear on a cold tumbler is answered by condensation, defined in 32735; 32733 only makes the observation.
Was 32731 (Ice and Water Are One Substance). The covered tumbler gaining mass on the balance is Activity 8.4 in 32736.

Was 32731 (Ice and Water Are One Substance), which only notes that water flows and ice does not. The shape comparison across states - ice keeping its shape, water taking the container's - is stated in 32738.
Was 32731 (Ice and Water Are One Substance). Another substance going liquid to solid is the candle wax and coconut oil of 32740, where melting and freezing are named.
Was 32731 (Ice and Water Are One Substance). Liquid water to solid ice is freezing, named in 32740.
Was 32739 (Collecting Water from Humid Air), the machine box. That water vapour exists invisibly in the air around us at room temperature is stated in 32738.

Was 32732 (Where the Water on the Plate Went), which is evaporation. A cool plate held over steam collecting droplets is condensation, defined in 32735; 32734 carries the same plate-over-boiling-water sighting as an unexplained case.
Was 32746 (The Water Cycle). Which states of water are commonly observed is section 8.3's three states, in 32737.
Was 32746 (The Water Cycle). Liquid to gas below boiling point is evaporation, which 32732 defines and says happens even at room temperature.
Was 32746 (The Water Cycle). That water vapour is lighter than air and therefore rises is the box inside 32745, which explains why the vapour goes up at all.
